valuation_philosophy: CDI is a land subdivider, not an operating cash-flow compounder: reported OCF/FCF has been structurally negative for three straight years (FY2023 -10.3m, FY2024 -8.1m, FY2025 -9.0m) because cash is being reinvested into growing the development-property land bank (inventory build), which is growth capex disguised as working capital, not distress. A Gordon-growth FCF DCF off that series would be meaningless. This model instead values CDI on (1) an EARNINGS-POWER basis -- discounting projected dividends plus a Year-5 exit value equal to Year-5 NPAT capitalised at an exit P/E -- and (2) an NTA/BOOK-VALUE basis -- discounting projected dividends plus a Year-5 exit value equal to Year-5 book NTA/share capitalised at a market-observed exit P/B multiple, since CDI's land bank (development property) is carried at the lower of cost and net realisable value and independent valuers assess it materially above carrying cost ($339.3m residential + $68.9m commercial vs a $275.5m residential carrying value at FY2025). The two legs are weighted 50/50 into a 'blended IV' per scenario, then probability-weighted 25/50/25 (bull/base/bear) into a single weighted IV. Exit multiples for BOTH legs are anchored to CDI's own trading history (Dec FY-end closes vs FY-end book NTA and EPS) rather than to an assumed re-rating, because the stock has a 10-year record to check assumptions against (see sanity_check). Interest income is stripped from the earnings base only insofar as it already sits inside NPAT and net cash is not separately added to avoid double counting -- net cash is inside book equity (NTA), which is the terminal-value base for the NTA leg, and inside the earnings retained into book value for the earnings leg, so grossing it up again on top of either exit value would double count the same balance-sheet cash. Stock-based compensation is verified NIL (no equity comp scheme) so no SBC adjustment is required or applied -- unadjusted and SBC-adjusted figures are identical here.

inputs.new_debt_facility: NZ$20m ANZ credit facility entered 7-Aug-2026 (first-ever debt facility; terms beyond amount/lender/date not disclosed). Not drawn as of FY2025 balance date, so FY2025 net debt figure above excludes it; flagged as a structural risk (see risks) and the reason net cash is NOT modelled as a growing pile going forward.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 OCF -8.99m less minor capex -0.025m. Structurally negative for 3 straight years from land-bank (inventory) reinvestment -- NOT an owner-FCF base for this business; see valuation_philosophy.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Not applicable -- this is an earnings + NTA model, not an FCF DCF. See fy2025_npat and nta_book_value_per_share instead.
inputs.sbc_source: Verified NIL -- CDI operates no employee equity/share-based compensation scheme. Adjusted and unadjusted figures are therefore identical; no SBC adjustment applied or required.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not separately stripped as a distinct FCF-model input since this is not an FCF DCF; interest income is embedded in reported NPAT (FY2025 sensitivity ~$0.12m per 1pp rate move on depleted cash balances per company disclosure) and is not double-counted because net cash is not separately added to either exit value (see valuation_philosophy).
inputs.mark_to_market_note: Memo only, NOT used as the DCF terminal-value base (which uses BOOK NTA against a market-observed P/B multiple) -- shown to illustrate the margin of safety embedded in historic-cost land carrying values. Investment/rental property is separately fair-valued under IAS 40 so no further uplift is assumed there.
inputs.annual_share_growth_source: Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP), active since 1998; historically issues ~0.3-1.0m shares/yr (277.5m FY2017 -> 292.7m FY2025). Modelled at a conservative flat 0.3%/yr.

historical_growth.mid_cycle_rationale: The 11-year mean ($25.17m) is inflated by the FY2019-2022 post-COVID housing boom (four consecutive years of $30-34m NPAT that will not repeat absent another synchronized rate-cut + migration + house-price cycle). The FY2023-2025 downturn trough ($11-15m) is equally unrepresentative on the low side. $20m is selected as the Year-5/steady-state anchor -- roughly halfway between the downturn trough and the boom peak, consistent with the low end of the prompt's suggested $18-22m band and with a business that has genuinely grown its land bank and rental income base since the prior mid-cycle (so a flat repeat of, say, FY2016-18's $27-33m range is not assumed, but nor is the boom high-water mark).
historical_growth.revenue_note: Revenue is not a meaningful DCF growth driver here -- it is settlement-timing lumpy (recognised only on Certificate of Title transfer) and structurally fell as Prestons Park (the flagship development) wound down through FY2025. NPAT is the growth-rate driver used.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (used only as a rough cross-check; the model itself is a bottom-up NPAT path + NTA roll-forward, not a growth-rate-extrapolated FCF DCF)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.3%) vs NPAT trend diverge sharply because FY2023-2025 NPAT collapsed 3.1x peak-to-trough while equity kept compounding on retained (lower) earnings plus DRP share issuance -- expected and consistent with a cyclical earner reinvesting into a slow-compounding asset base; not a data-quality flag.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is NIL so there is no SBC-vs-FCF divergence to report for this ticker.

wacc_rationale.cyclicality_premium_note: 3.1x peak-to-trough NPAT swing (FY2019 $34.1m to FY2025 $11.1m) is extreme even for a cyclical developer.
wacc_rationale.illiquidity_premium_note: Only ~27% free float once MCK (65.12%) and Adrian Ho (8.14%) are excluded; 2,376 holders but top 13 control 85.27% of the register.
wacc_rationale.control_premium_note: Majority control by MCK/Hong Leong (65.12%) effectively removes takeover optionality and gives minority holders no influence over capital allocation, dividend policy or board composition beyond the independent-director majority.
wacc_rationale.concentration_premium_note: Land bank concentrated in Hamilton/Ruakura 2 (46%, largely unconsented) and Hawke's Bay/Havelock North (26%, one Fast-track application already rejected at council level).
wacc_rationale.note: CDI carries essentially no debt (FY2025: $0.056m total debt vs $321.178m equity), so cost of equity and WACC converge -- the discount rate above is used as both. The new Aug-2026 NZ$20m ANZ facility is small relative to the balance sheet and not yet drawn, so it is not modelled as materially shifting the capital structure, but its existence is folded qualitatively into the control/financial-risk premium already in the stack and flagged in risks.

base.npat_path_rationale: Year 1 (FY2026) set below FY2025's $11.1m per explicit AGM (26-May-2026) guidance that FY2026 earnings will be 'considerably lower.' Years 2-5 recover gradually toward the $20m mid-cycle anchor as the NZ housing cycle turns, OCR eases from 2.25%, and the Fast-track pipeline (Arataki Road first sections late-2027, Ruakura 2 lodgement targeted end-2026) begins contributing.
base.payout_rationale: FY2025 actual payout was 26.4% (1.0 cps fully imputed on 3.78 cps EPS); held roughly flat, consistent with the Board's stated capital-retention discipline while funding the Fast-track pipeline and (now) servicing the new debt facility.
base.exit_multiple_rationale: Exit P/B anchored to CDI's own FY2022-2025 trading regime (actual Dec-close P/B range 0.693-0.742x, average 0.714x) -- i.e. assumes the market continues to price CDI the same way it has for the last four years, NOT a re-rating. Exit P/E of 10.0x is cross-checked for consistency: at a ~5.6% mid-cycle ROE ($20m NPAT / ~$360m average equity), P/B 0.71x implies a consistent P/E of ~12.8x (P/E = P/B / ROE), so 10.0x is if anything conservative relative to that cross-check.

bull.npat_path_rationale: Faster-than-base recovery: Fast-track pipeline (Ruakura 2's ~1,350 lots, Arataki Road, Iona Stage 3) delivers on schedule, OCR cuts restore purchaser confidence sooner, and the growing rental leg (currently 9.4% of revenue) provides an earlier earnings floor. Year-5 NPAT approaches but stays below the FY2019-2022 boom peak ($30-34m).
bull.exit_multiple_rationale: Modest re-rating toward the 10-year historical AVERAGE P/B (0.959x, we use 0.90x conservatively below that average) as Fast-track delivery de-risks the pipeline and the debt-free premium is restored post any early repayment of the ANZ facility.

bear.npat_path_rationale: Downturn is deeper and more prolonged than management's 'considerably lower' guidance implies; geopolitical/employment/migration headwinds persist, Iona Stage 3-style council rejections recur elsewhere in the Fast-track pipeline, and Year-5 NPAT only reaches the FY2023-2024 trough-recovery range, not mid-cycle.
bear.exit_multiple_rationale: De-rating below the recent 4-year trading floor (0.693x), reflecting the erosion of the 'debt-free' balance-sheet premium now that CDI carries its first-ever debt facility, plus continued minority/illiquidity discount in a weak macro tape.

entry_price.methodology: PV of Year1-5 base-case dividends at 15% + PV of the Year-5 blended exit value (50% NTA-leg exit at WACC-consistent P/B 0.71x, 50% earnings-leg exit at WACC-consistent P/E 10.0x) discounted back at 15%, divided by the Year-5 projected share count. Net cash is NOT added separately -- it already sits inside book equity (NTA), which is the basis for both exit values, so adding it again would double count the same balance-sheet cash (see valuation_philosophy).

base.note: Entry price ($0.430) sits ABOVE the base-case intrinsic value ($0.396), which is the mirror image of the usual pattern -- because CDI's structural WACC (17%) EXCEEDS the generic 15% hurdle rate (reflecting the cyclicality/illiquidity/control premiums stacked in wacc_rationale), discounting at 15% instead of 17% is LESS punitive, so entry price is naturally higher than WACC-based intrinsic value here. Both remain well below the current $0.65 market price.

sensitivity.note: This is not a Gordon-growth FCF DCF, so the sensitivity axes are WACC and the Year-5 exit multiple (P/B, with a proportionally-scaled exit P/E) rather than WACC and terminal growth.

sanity_check.methodology: Matched Dec (fiscal year-end) monthly closes from Yahoo Finance (10y range) against FY-end book NTA/share (ShareholdersEquity / SharesOutstanding) and EPS to compute actual historical P/B and P/E for every complete FY 2017-2025.
sanity_check.note_on_prompt_assumption: The task brief assumed CDI 'has essentially NEVER traded above ~1.0x book' -- the actual matched Dec-close history shows this is true only for the FY2022-2025 downturn/higher-rate regime (P/B 0.693-0.742x, avg 0.714x). In the earlier FY2017-2021 up-cycle the stock traded at 1.07-1.40x book. This model deliberately anchors exit multiples to the RECENT 4-year regime (0.60-0.90x across bear/base/bull), not the older boom-era range, because the boom-era multiples reflect a rate/migration/house-price environment management explicitly says has not returned (FY2026 guided 'considerably lower' than an already-depressed FY2025).
sanity_check.verdict: PASS -- no overvaluation trip. Base-case implied P/B (0.347x) and implied forward P/E (13.1x) both sit comfortably BELOW their respective historical ceilings (1.5x max P/B = 2.10x; 2x avg P/E = 22.5x). If anything the base-case IV implies a P/B (0.347x) even below the entire 10-year trading floor (0.693x), which is a legitimate but noteworthy result of a 17% structural WACC discounting a low-growth (~5%/yr NTA/share) book-value compounder over a 5-year horizon -- discount-rate-exceeds-growth-rate mechanics mechanically produce a large PV haircut even when the EXIT multiple assumption is simply held flat at the stock's own recent trading regime (0.71x). No fix was applied because the check is designed to catch overvaluation (implied multiples running ABOVE history), not undervaluation, and both trip conditions are false. SBC is nil for CDI so adjusted and unadjusted multiples are identical -- no SBC correction is applicable here.
sanity_check.cross_check_market_implied_discount_rate: Solving the base-case NTA leg for the discount rate that reproduces the current $0.65 price (holding the same NPAT path, payout ratio and 0.71x exit P/B) gives ~8.2% -- well below even the unstressed NZ small-cap base rate (11.5%) used in wacc_rationale. This means the market is EITHER (a) implicitly using a materially lower discount rate than the risk premia stacked here justify, (b) pricing in a Year-1 NPAT recovery milder than this model's guided-down $8.5m, or (c) simply mispricing CDI at a discount to its own risk-adjusted intrinsic value, consistent with the persistent minority/illiquidity discount documented across the ownership structure. Reported for transparency, not as a model input.
